about: Copy changes the lead decided on (FIX_BRIEF, 2026-10-17): D1 homepage and shared headings, D6 minimal factual corrections, D5's split of the one-block Ahwatukee body, D7's review count in the business description, D13's ROC lookup site, and the owner's decisions of 2026-10-19: D15 generator mentions out, D16 every conflicting price set to the higher figure, D17 one plain warranty line. Same format as the slop files; these run after them, so an edit here may change a slop edit's new text.

edits.old_text: Electrician solutions tailored to your needs
edits.new_text: Electrical work we do, from repairs to EV chargers
edits.reason: D1: stock heading ("solutions tailored to your needs") over the What we do checklist; the replacement is the slop-pages review's suggestion. The homepage title and H1 stay frozen.
D1: the highlighted words follow the new heading (as slop-pages-043 does on /commercial-electrician).

edits.old_text: Let our reviews speak for themselves
edits.reason: D1: cliché heading; the same replacement as slop-pages-045 on /commercial-electrician.
D1: the highlighted words follow the new heading.

edits.old_text: We proudly serve the entire valley!
edits.new_text: We serve the entire Phoenix valley
edits.reason: D1: "proudly serve" plus exclamation; the same line as slop-pages-018, -032 and -036 on the pages that reuse this section.
D1: the highlighted words follow the new heading.
D1: "Solutions" filler in a capability title (homepage checklist and the 404 page's list); the link to the Custom Lighting service is unchanged.
D1: "Solutions" filler in a capability title; the replacement is the slop-pages review's suggestion.

D1: stock benefit title, replaced with a plain one from the card's own text ("We'll tackle your problems big or small"). Not "Done right the first time": the section heading right above says that, and the card's text ends with it.

edits.new_text: We come back if anything's wrong
edits.reason: D1: stock benefit title. The card already makes the claim: "we'll always come back if you have any issues" (live copy, kept by slop-pages-012). Straight apostrophe like the card's own text.

edits.old_text: We're ready to work for you
edits.new_text: You'll know the price before we start
edits.reason: D1: the shared closing band's heading (every page with the estimate band) was a stock line. The replacement is the business's flat-rate promise from /faq: "we quote you a price before we start and that's what you pay". The band's eyebrow says "Free estimates" and its button "Get a Free Estimate".

D6: ASU's football stadium has been "Mountain America Stadium, Home of the ASU Sun Devils" since the naming-rights deal of 2023-08-02 (ASU News, news.asu.edu/20230802-university-news-asu-mountain-america-credit-union-naming-rights-deal-football-stadium; Sun Devil Athletics, thesundevils.com/facilities-venues/mountain-america-stadium, checked 2026-10-17). Applies to slop-cities-056's sentence.

edits.old_text: A Level 1 charger works by converting AC power from a regular outlet into DC power
edits.new_text: A Level 1 charger delivers AC power from a regular outlet, which the car’s onboard charger converts into DC power
edits.reason: D6: a Level 1 (or Level 2) charger supplies AC; the conversion to DC happens in the car's onboard charger. The rest of the sentence and its citation are unchanged.
D6: house wiring at 120 V is line voltage, not high voltage.
D6: as D6-03; applies to slop-posts-b-124's sentence.

D7 (citations R5, amended): the Mesa Google Business Profile shows 5.0 from 567 reviews on 2026-10-17, so the count reads 560+ wherever it is stated. Applies to slop-pages-069's new text, as R5 asks; Site settings' reviewSummary.reviewCount comes from migration/content-data/profiles.json.

edits.old_text: which you can verify at azroc.gov
edits.new_text: which you can verify at roc.az.gov
edits.reason: D13 (citations R6, amended): roc.az.gov is the Registrar of Contractors' own host (www.azroc.gov 301s to it). The link in "How do I choose a good electrician in Phoenix?" now points there (linkFixes in migration/content-data/cms-templates.json), so this answer names the same site.

edits.old_text: leaving homes with partial power or dangerous backfeed issues if a generator is installed incorrectly.
edits.reason: D15 (owner, 2026-10-19: "remove generator"): the business does not do generator work. The clause about generators installed wrongly goes; the downed-lines point stays.

D15 (owner, 2026-10-19: "remove generator"): the business does not do generator work. The "Don’t DIY Generator Hookups" tip (heading and text, D15-03) told readers to have a pro install their generator; the other storm-protection tips stay.

edits.old_text: If you’re using a generator, improper wiring can backfeed into the grid and cause deadly hazards. Always have a pro install it.
edits.reason: D15 (owner, 2026-10-19: "remove generator"): the business does not do generator work. The text under the heading D15-02 removes.
D15 (owner, 2026-10-19: "remove generator"): the business does not do generator work. "Generator installation & hookup" is taken off the "We offer" list.

edits.old_text: Installing a generator or EV charger
edits.reason: D15 (owner, 2026-10-19: "remove generator"): the business does not do generator work. The list of work that needs a permit names only work the business does. Tier 1 post: body only; its title, meta and H1 do not change.

edits.old_text: Outages are frequent too, and a backup generator can carry you through them.
edits.reason: D15 (owner, 2026-10-19: "remove generator"): the business does not do generator work. The backup-generator suggestion goes; the outage fact under "Power Surges and Outages" stays. Applies to slop-posts-a-090's new text.

D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): whole-house surge protector, installed. /faq said $300–$600; /blog-posts/whole-house-surge-protector-guide-arizona and /blog-posts/is-whole-house-surge-protection-necessary say $400–$800, so the FAQ takes $400–$800. Applies to slop-pages-066's new text.

D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): six recessed LED lights in an existing (finished) ceiling, all in. /faq said $1,050–$1,750; /blog-posts/recessed-lighting-installation-phoenix says $1,400–$2,200 for six lights on a finished ceiling, so the FAQ takes $1,400–$2,200. The recessed service's priceRange follows (D16-10).

D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): a Level 2 home charger, installed. This post said $600–$2,500; /faq and the EV service's priceRange say $750–$3,500. The installation-only figure ($400–$1,700) and the unit price ($160–$2,000) are parts of the total, not the same price, and stay.
D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): the "Typical Cost Range" cell for Level 2 in the Technical Specifications table, as D16-03.

D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): a Level 1 charger. The post said $80–$180 in two places and $300–$600 in its Technical Specifications table ("Typical Cost Range"); both now read $300–$600.
D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): the Cost Overview line for Level 1, as D16-05.

D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): a 200-amp panel. This post said $1,800–$2,500; /faq, the panels service priceRange and every panel post say $5,200–$6,500 for a standard 200-amp panel (owner question 4 in migration/content-edits/README.md).

D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): installing a fan on existing wiring and a fan-rated box. The same post says $150–$350 under "The Short Answer"; the replacement section now matches it.

edits.old_text: typically $2,500 to $5,000 for a whole house
edits.new_text: typically $3,000 to $7,000 for a whole house
edits.reason: D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): whole-house aluminum wiring remediation with AlumiConn connectors. This post said $2,500–$5,000; /blog-posts/aluminum-wiring-older-phoenix-homes says $3,000–$7,000 for the same method. Tier 1 post: body only.
D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): the recessed service's priceRange (structured data only; service pages show no price) follows the FAQ figure D16-02 sets.

edits.old_text: a full rewire costs between $8,000 and $15,000.
edits.new_text: a full rewire costs between $12,000 and $25,000.
edits.reason: D16 (owner, 2026-10-19: "Always go with the higher amounts"): a full house rewire. This post said $8,000–$15,000 for a typical single-story home; /blog-posts/aluminum-wiring-older-phoenix-homes gives $12,000–$25,000+ and calls it the same as any whole-home rewire, pointing to this guide. The size breakdown below it is left as published (no figures were invented); the owner is asked to confirm it. Tier 1 post: body only.

edits.old_text: Yes, we do. We offer a 2-year warranty on services we provide. Contact us for full warranty details.
edits.new_text: Yes. Our work comes with a warranty.
edits.reason: D17 (owner, 2026-10-19: "lets not talk about warranty but just say work comes w/ a warranty"): the answer says the work comes with a warranty and nothing more: no term, no conditions, no "contact us for details" (its "Contact us" link goes with the sentence). The question stays; the answer shows on /faq and /our-team.

edits.old_text: and we'll always come back if you have any issues.
edits.new_text: and we'll always come back if you have any issues. Our work comes with a warranty.
edits.reason: D17 (owner, 2026-10-19: "lets not talk about warranty but just say work comes w/ a warranty"): the homepage card "We come back if anything's wrong" (Site settings → value props) gains the one plain line. No term or conditions.

splits.reason:
D5: the Webflow export holds Ahwatukee's whole article in one block, its paragraphs and neighbourhood list separated by line breaks, so it rendered as one paragraph full of
s. After the slop-cities edits it becomes one block per paragraph, and the neighbourhoods a bullet list under their bold label, like the other nine cities.
